articles.title: "Being bullied....": Donna Kelce reveals the one important lesson she taught Travis and Jason Kelce that shaped their characters
articles.summary: Donna Kelce had never wanted her sons to stand by and watch when someone needed help.
articles.body: Donna Kelce had never wanted her sons to stand by and watch when someone needed help. Long before Travis and Jason Kelce became two of the NFL's most recognisable names, she had taught them that kindness mattered more than popularity. In a May 8, 2024, appearance on The Martha Stewart Podcast, Donna opened up about the values she had instilled in her children and recalled how their willingness to protect others sometimes landed them in trouble at school.Donna Kelce recalled how Travis and Jason stood up to bulliesFor Donna Kelce, raising two boys who would eventually become professional football players was never just about building confidence or encouraging competition. She wanted Travis Kelce and Jason to understand that everyone deserved respect, regardless of their position in life.Explaining the lesson she repeatedly shared with her sons, Donna said, "I think the importance of being loyal to your friends, that you be kind to everyone. That no matter if somebody's at school and it's the individual that's cleaning the toilets, or if it's a principal or a teacher or somebody that has a disability, that you treat everyone equally and with respect. I think that's the most important thing."Her advice went beyond asking them to be polite. Donna wanted her boys to recognise when someone was being treated unfairly and have the courage to intervene.She continued, "And if you see someone in trouble, help you know. And if you see somebody that's being bullied or anything like that, try and step in and get in between that person. Because they were big, so they could make a difference and make sure that that child was okay."Donna Kelce explained why she defended her sons at schoolTravis and Jason did not always stay out of trouble while following their mother's advice. Their willingness to protect other children sometimes meant Donna had to visit the principal's office.However, she did not believe every school incident deserved punishment without understanding what had happened. If her sons had stepped in to protect someone, she was prepared to support their decision.Recalling those moments, Donna said, "So they did that a lot, and sometimes they went a little crazy. And so I was in the principal's office and I'm like, look, they were helping this kid out who was being bullied. And I said, I'll stand behind that every day of the week."Her words offered a glimpse into the family values that shaped both brothers. Their mother understood that standing up for someone was not always easy, especially when it meant facing consequences.For Donna, the lesson was simple. She would rather explain why her sons defended a vulnerable child than teach them to ignore someone else's struggle.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Hitting the Powerball’… Kansas City Chiefs star has never had it so good, says Ryan Clark
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ newest receiving weapon showed up immediately against the Atlanta Falcons. Chiefs general manager Brett Veach provided a surprise for...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs' newest receiving weapon showed up immediately against the Atlanta Falcons.

Chiefs general manager Brett Veach provided a surprise for quarterback Patrick Mahomes at the NFL trade deadline, agreeing a trade for Josh Downs.

Downs was traded away by the Indianapolis Colts to the Chiefs for a fourth and fifth round pick, a move that could end up looking like a bargain.

The new Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver made an instant impact in Week 10 in his first game for his new team.

Downs caught his first touchdown from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter, catching an 18-yard pass in the endzone.

NFL expert Ryan Clark reacted to Downs' first Chiefs touchdown by reflecting on the incredible turnaround in fortunes for the receiver – after leaving the 2-7 Colts.

Clark posted on social media: "Man, imagine going to sleep one week with Daniel Jones as your QB, and waking up the next with Patrick Mahomes!

"That's the football version of hitting the Powerball! I know Josh Downs feels like a new man!"

Downs leaves a losing team for a winning team

Josh Downs had requested a trade away from the Indianapolis Colts after their poor start to the season, and clear intention to rebuild.

His Colts team were 2-7 heading into Week 10, while the Chiefs were 6-2 prior to their win over the Falcons.

Downs has never played a game in the NFL Playoffs during his three seasons in Indianapolis.

Now providing he can stay injury-free in Kansas City, Downs will likely finally get the chance to play in the postseason with the Chiefs.

It's hard to disagree with Ryan Clark's assessment that he has 'won the Powerball' with the trade.

articles.title: Dianna Russini opens up about 'heartbreaking' six months after Mike Vrabel scandal, reveals how NFL players urged her to return
articles.summary: Dianna Russini has opened up about the difficult months she spent away from sports media after the controversy involving New England Patriots head coach
articles.body: Dianna Russini has opened up about the difficult months she spent away from sports media after the controversy involving New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. The former NFL reporter said staying at her New Jersey home with her husband, Kevin Goldschmidt, and their two sons gave her a chance to rethink her priorities and focus on her family. Now, seven months after leaving The Athletic, Russini has returned to football coverage with a new show, The Russini Report, on BetUS TV. During its November 11 debut, she also spoke about the support she received from NFL players and people around the league.How did Dianna Russini spend her months away from NFL reporting?Russini began the first episode of her new show with a personal message about the time she spent away from work. Rather than going straight into football news, she spoke about how being at home helped her look at her life differently.“Over the last few months, I have had a lot of time to think about my life and my priorities and the person that I want to be moving forward, and being home in New Jersey with my husband and our two little boys and being truly present, it gave me so much perspective that I didn’t even know I needed,” Russini said.Her comments offered a glimpse into how she spent the months following her departure from The Athletic. The reporter, who had been a familiar face in NFL coverage, stepped away from her regular work after photographs of her with Vrabel at an Arizona resort became public.The time away also allowed her to spend more time with Goldschmidt and their children. Russini did not go into every detail of what happened during those months, but made it clear that being with her family had become an important part of her life.Why did Dianna Russini and Kevin Goldschmidt delete their social media accounts?The months following the controversy were particularly difficult for Russini and her husband. Both decided to delete their X accounts after finding it increasingly hard to deal with the comments and claims being made about them online.In an interview with PEOPLE, Russini explained why they chose to step away from social media. She did not want the online discussion to become another problem for her family while they were already dealing with a difficult situation.“This was a runaway train, and there was nothing I could do to stop it. Once we realized nothing was going to stop this, it became unhealthy for us to read it because it wasn’t helping us heal. It was piling on and adding to what we were already dealing with.”She also spoke about the emotional effect of the entire episode, saying, “The best way to describe what the last six months were like for me is heartbreaking.”Russini had earlier described the situation as a nightmare. Her decision to stay away from social media gave her and Goldschmidt some distance from the constant discussion surrounding the photographs.How did NFL players support Dianna Russini during her break?Although Russini stepped away from her regular reporting work, she said she did not lose contact with people in the NFL. In fact, she credited the league and its players with helping her feel connected to football during a period when she was not working.She said people from the NFL regularly checked on her, not just to discuss football but also to ask how she was doing personally.“The absolute best part of this situation has been the loyalty the NFL has shown me. They checked in with me almost daily while I wasn’t working to make sure that I was staying connected to football, to check on me as a person and to just see how I was doing,” she said.Russini also revealed that several players contacted her directly and encouraged her to return to work. Their messages meant a lot to her, especially because she had spent years reporting on athletes who faced difficult moments in their careers.“I felt like players were texting and calling me to say, ‘Get back to work, it’s time,’” she said.She then explained how those conversations changed the way she looked at her own situation.“I think it’s pretty poetic that here I was all these years telling the story about these players going through adversity, and then they became sort of the people that I was learning from during this,” she added.For someone who had spent much of her career reporting on the NFL, hearing those words from players gave her another reason to return to the job.What happened between Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel?The controversy began after Page Six published photographs of Russini and Mike Vrabel together at the Ambiente resort in Sedona, Arizona. The pictures, taken on March 28, 2026, showed the NFL reporter and the Patriots coach hugging, holding hands and spending time together near the resort’s pool and hot tub.Both initially pushed back against suggestions that anything inappropriate had happened. Vrabel told the New York Post, “These photos show a completely innocent interaction and any suggestion otherwise is laughable. This doesn’t deserve any further response.”Russini also defended the photographs, saying, “The photos don’t represent the group of six people who were hanging out during the day. Like most journalists in the NFL, reporters interact with sources away from stadiums and other venues.”However, the situation became more difficult for Russini after The Athletic began an internal investigation into the matter. On April 14, she announced her resignation before her contract was due to end on June 30.In her resignation letter to executive editor Steven Ginsberg, she wrote, “I have covered the NFL with professionalism and dedication throughout my career, and I stand behind every story I have ever published.”She also explained her decision to leave, writing, “I do so not because I accept the narrative that has been constructed around this episode, but because I refuse to lend it further oxygen or to let it define me or my career.”The Athletic completed its investigation in September. As reported by Reuters, the outlet said Russini should have disclosed the nature of her relationship with Vrabel so editors could assess whether any reporting assignments involved a possible conflict of interest.Vrabel also addressed the situation publicly. In April, he announced that he would seek counseling and spend time with his family. He said, “I have always wanted to lead by example, and I believe this is what I have to do to be the best husband, father and coach that I possibly can be.”Russini’s return to sports media marks a new professional chapter. Her first show faced technical problems and started around 45 minutes late, with BetUS blaming the delay on a record-breaking audience. Once the programme began, she focused on NFL discussions rather than directly addressing the controversy.Her new show will cover NFL news, game analysis and her personal opinions, giving her a different way to continue working in football.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings are reunited and it feels so good after win over Green Bay Packers
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins led the Minnesota Vikings to a dominant win at Lambeau Field, and his emotional reunion with Kevin O'Connell raises a big question.
articles.body: We found out a lot about Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday because it is hard to add a new quarterback on a Tuesday, have him in full practices only two days during the week, and by week's end win a game in the same venue where he tore his Achilles three years ago. All that happened Sunday when the Minnesota Vikings beat the Green Bay Packers. But of all the things we learned from this game, maybe the most important is that Cousins and the Vikings maybe should not have broken up a couple of years ago. Perhaps they shouldn't have gone looking for greener pastures, shouldn't have believed for better outcomes, should not have quit on each other and the pretty good thing they had. VIKINGS ACQUIRE KIRK COUSINS FROM RAIDERS WHO TURN TO FERNANDO MENDOZA AS THEIR STARTING QB The Vikings and Cousins are together again. They're reunited and after winning in Lambeau Field, and they both feel so good. "It's been a blast to do ball with him again," coach Kevin O'Connell said afterward. "Football's an emotional game, and my football journey goes way back, and, you know, there's been highs and lows," Cousins told reporters after the victory. "And there's more of the story to write up ahead, but the last three years since being here have been a tough three years. "And, there's a lot of gratitude right now for being in this group again." The story of the misguided direction perhaps began in 2023 when Cousins tore his Achilles at Lambeau Field. Unable to overcome the injury by delivering a good season in 2026, the Vikings and Cousins went their different directions in March of 2024. Cousins went to the Atlanta Falcons as a high-priced free agent, believing he could ultimately finish his career there. But that changed weeks after signing him, the Falcons drafted Michael Penix Jr. in the first round of the draft and anointed the rookie their starter before that very season was over. Cousins sat much of 2025, and then went to the Raiders last offseason knowing he was keeping the starter's seat warm for Fernando Mendoza. Little did he know that seat would be pulled out from under him last week. MINNESOTA VIKINGS' SOFT BENCHING OF KYLER MURRAY LEADS TO CARSON WENTZ TAKING OVER AS NEW STARTING QB The Vikings? They didn't move on from Cousins to live happily ever after. When Cousins left in 2024, the Vikings thought replacing him wasn't an issue. They had found Sam Darnold in 2024, they were getting ready to draft J.J. McCarthy in the first round, and there was a certain arrogance within the organization that they could find someone, anyone, and turn him into a treasure. VIKINGS QUARTERBACK BATTLE MEETS EXPECTED END AS KYLER MURRAY BEATS OUT JJ MCCARTHY FOR STARTING JOB But then Darnold left. And McCarthy didn't work out. And Carson Wentz didn't work out, and Kyler Murray didn't work out earlier this season. And after those missteps, the Vikings decided last week that Cousins was their best option once again – just as he'd been from 2018 to 2023. And Cousin showed he's all of that in this one game. Cousins was already an upgrade by the time the Vikings held a 20-0 lead in the third quarter and scored twice more when the Packers tried to rally. And, yes, we know ... That is not exactly Super Bowl caliber quarterback play we saw from Cousins, because he did throw an interception and he still has to clean up some stuff. But having Cousins at quarterback clearly raised the Vikings' hopes. Justin Jefferson played with energy again. The offense could run the ball better because the Packers had to respect the passing game. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! And the defense that is among the best in the NFL sacked Jordan Love eight times – the most by any team in a game this season – because the unit was in the mostly unfamiliar spot of playing with a lead. "I thought for one of the first times this year, we played complimentary football," O'Connell said. Cousins was careful when it was over to remind everyone that the story of his return and this Vikings' season is not fully written. But we have a good start to the tale: It begins with the fact this combination maybe would have been better off staying together. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: 5-touchdown reminder: Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs are alive and well
articles.summary: Mahomes threw five touchdown passes in a game for the first time since 2022 in blowout victory over the Falcons.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — He's lurking. While the rest of the NFL universe is falling all over itself praising Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, while everyone's anointing the Chicago Bears and the Jacksonville Jaguars as the new kings of the NFL, Patrick Mahomes is still quietly on the prowl. Or, was .

After Sunday's spectacular performance — five touchdowns and 348 yards passing in a 35-13 road win over Atlanta — Mahomes and the Chiefs are flat-out rolling, even with an aging core and an array of new arrivals and rookies. Kansas City missed the playoffs last January after Mahomes was lost for the season, and he's already taken hits this year that have Chiefs fans twitching . Only a handful of starting quarterbacks — guys like Rodgers, Prescott, Cousins, Stafford and Goff — are older than the 31-year-old Mahomes. And yet, when he's slinging it like he did Sunday, it feels like he's never going away, either.

"He's a luxury to have and to coach," Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said after the game. "He does an excellent job of spreading around and using all of his receivers. He's not afraid to use any of them. You don't see a lot of that around the league."

KC pushed around Denver in Week 1, then beefed up on high-calorie opponents like Indianapolis, Miami, Las Vegas and the Los Angeles Chargers. When Kansas City faced some tougher opposition — Seattle and Denver on the road — the Chiefs folded. Atlanta wouldn't be a playoff-caliber team in any respectable division, but still … you can't argue with five touchdowns to four different receivers, including one who just joined the Chiefs a few days ago.

Josh Downs, who arrived in Kansas City via a trade-deadline deal with Indianapolis, took all of a single half to get into rhythm with Mahomes, scoring his first touchdown in a Chiefs uniform with 18 seconds remaining in the first half.

"Our new guy, Downs, it looks like there's a connection there, right?" Reid said with a smile. "They worked well today, and that's on two days of practice."

"We haven't got a ton of reps, and that's why there's some times you're going to see on tape [from Sunday] where he was open and I didn't give him chances," Mahomes said. "But whenever you do it in the game, that's the best reps to get. I'll be able to have that trust as the season goes on."

Downs finished the day with four receptions, 53 yards and a touchdown. Also in the mix: Cyrus Allen with 44 yards and a touchdown, Andrew Armstrong with 43 yards and also a touchdown, and Rashee Rice with a team-leading 82 yards. Travis Kelce, Mahomes' career-long security blanket, had two catches for 30 yards, separated by a quick trip into the locker room after a hard tackle .

"Kells [Kelce] left for a bit with a calf," Reid said. "He's been battling this ankle. … Kind of landed on it that first catch and twisted up a little bit." Reid didn't indicate there was anything more serious with the Chiefs' most tabloid-famous player, and from a football perspective, Mahomes now has the luxury of relying on half a dozen receivers who aren't Travis Kelce.

"More than anything, [Sunday] proves that we can attack down the field like we believe that we can," Mahomes said. "If [defenses] are going to come down and try to stop the run, we have to prove that we can throw it down the field. It just showcases another level to our offense that we can continue to get better and better."

Here's what makes Kansas City even more dangerous. Mahomes knew he had to shoulder a heavier load than usual Sunday with Kenneth Walker III out with a groin injury. What he probably wasn't expecting, however, was the sudden and explosive emergence of rookie Emmett Johnson, who rushed for 101 yards and hauled in 70 yards' worth of Mahomes passes for two touchdowns on the afternoon.

"I'm so happy for him because he comes in with the right mindset every single day. He has a smile on his face, he wants to be great, he wants to contribute in any way possible," Mahomes said. "Obviously, with having Kenneth and how great he's playing, he hasn't got as many opportunities. But when his number got called, he stepped in and made the plays happen. That's going to be great to have as the season goes on and we get Kenneth back as that one-two punch."

Part of the hesitation to commit to the Chiefs as a bona fide contender is the status of Mahomes' elbow. He suffered a hit during last week's game against the Jets that had him hanging his arm by his side, although he stayed in the game. ESPN reported Sunday morning that the Chiefs had consulted with elbow specialists from the Kansas City Royals and Texas Rangers, both of whom signed off on Mahomes' Sunday start.

"I was a little nervous going into the game just because it was a little sore," he said. "I didn't feel like during the week of practice I was driving the ball the way I wanted [on] some of those deeper in-cut routes and getting the balls down the field. You don't know until you get out there and that adrenaline starts kicking a little bit. Obviously, it was good enough."

Two of Mahomes' receivers, Armstrong and Allen, recorded their first career touchdowns on Sunday, a fact that didn't escape Mahomes' attention. "Playing in the NFL is a dream … you never know if you're ever going to get that first touchdown when you get here," he said. "I still know exactly where my first touchdown football is, and I know how important it is to me whenever people come to the house and ask about it."

After both touchdowns, Mahomes raced downfield and made sure to secure the footballs for the two rookies. "When you score, you're just celebrating, you're not really paying attention to what's going on," he said. "So I just made sure to grab that so that they have that memory, because they've worked their entire life to be here. They get in the end zone. Not a lot of people get to do that, and so they'll have that for the rest of their life."

And they had Patrick Mahomes throw it to them, a fact that becomes more impressive by the year.

articles.title: Cowboys' Defense Makes Wrong Kind of History as McCaffrey, Samuel Score Huge TDs for 49ers
articles.summary: It's no secret that the Dallas Cowboys' defense has struggled mightily in 2026, and those struggles led to them making a dubious kind of history on Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers.
articles.body:
It's no secret that the Dallas Cowboys' defense has struggled mightily in 2026, and those struggles led to them making a dubious kind of history on Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers.

Christian McCaffrey scored on a 74-yard touchdown pass, and Deebo Samuel later scored on a 70-yard run. It marked the first time the Cowboys have allowed a 70-plus-yard touchdown pass and a 70-plus-yard touchdown run in the same game.

McCaffrey added a 66-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter to help give his team some cushion:

Dallas came into Sunday's contest allowing the third-most yards per game (372.7) and the seventh-most points per game (26.2). Those numbers didn't get any better on Sunday, as they allowed 46 points and 584 yards.

The Cowboys' offense has been solid for the most part, putting up the sixth-most points per game (27.3), so it's fair to blame the defense for the 4-5 start to the 2026 campaign.

Dallas' playoff hopes are still alive, mostly thanks to a weak NFC East, but it can't afford to keep giving up massive plays on defense as it did on Sunday.

articles.title: Mendoza's 1st Start Spoiled, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Top Raiders & Seahawks Players
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza's first start for the Las Vegas Raiders was spoiled by Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks, taking a 21-13 loss at home.
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza's first start for the Las Vegas Raiders was spoiled by Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks, taking a 21-13 loss at home.

The defending champions entered the matchup against the Raiders as 6.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , improving to 6-4 with the win while Las Vegas fell to 4-6.

Last year's Heisman Trophy winner made his first start after the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 10 in exchange for a 2027 third-round draft pick.

In his debut, he finished with 143 passing yards, completed 59 percent of his passes and rushed for one touchdown.

After an opening-drive fumble by the Seahawks, the Raiders closed out the first quarter with a 34-yard touchdown pass from Lock to Cooper Kupp to tie the game after Mendoza rushed up the middle for his first NFL touchdown.

The Raiders added a field goal in the second quarter to take a 10-7 lead into halftime.

The Seahawks mounted a comeback in the third quarter, scoring two touchdowns while holding Las Vegas scoreless.

Jadarian Price rushed for a touchdown before Lock connected with Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 71-yard touchdown pass to give Seattle a 21-10 lead entering the fourth quarter.

Despite a costly fourth quarter that included a fumble and a missed field goal by the Seahawks, the Raiders could not put together a game-winning drive. Las Vegas managed a field goal before Seattle ran out the clock to seal the win.

The Raiders will hit the road to face the Denver Broncos next Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, while the Seahawks head into their bye week.

articles.title: Bijan Robinson Admits Falcons 'Deserve' Boos After Blowout Loss to Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons' offense received boos on Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs despite playing at home.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons' offense received boos on Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs despite playing at home.

Star running back Bijan Robinson couldn't blame his team's fans.

"They put in their hard-earned work every single week to try to make it to these games, and it's our job to make it count for them," Robinson said after the 35-13 loss, per ESPN's Marc Raimondi . "So yeah, when they boo us, we deserve it."

The Falcons appeared ready to turn the corner after a 29-20 upset win over the San Francisco 49ers in Week 7, but the offense has since turned in three rough performances.

Atlanta was shut out by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8 before scoring 17 points in a loss to the Cincinnati Bengals last week.

On Sunday, quarterback Michael Penix Jr. threw for 286 yards and an interception on 23-of-43 passing, and the Falcons netted just 100 yards on the ground. Robinson had 16 carries for 71 yards and a touchdown.

Atlanta converted just five of its 16 third downs and went 1-for-5 in the red zone. The Falcons started the game with four straight three-and-outs, which Raimondi noted was the first time they'd done so since 2000.

"The responsibility falls on me," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said. "All of this falls on me. So, I'll take responsibility for everything that goes on in this football team. We all have to be better. That's the truth. We will all learn from it, not going to hide from it, going to own it and then make corrections."

It's not the first time this season the Falcons have been booed by their home crowd, as they were also met with hostility from Mercedes-Benz Stadium during a 34-3 loss to the Carolina Panthers in Week 2.

The Falcons are competing in a weak NFC South and had a prime opportunity to snap an eight-year playoff drought, but after a 3-7 start, the postseason is seemingly more and more unlikely.

articles.title: Aidan Hutchinson's knee injury joins ranks of infamous NFL celebration injuries, including Bill Gramatica, Gus Frerotte running head-first into a wall
articles.summary: Hutchinson wasn't the first player to sustain a significant injury while celebrating. he won't be the last.
articles.body:
The All-Pro Detroit Lions pass rusher sustained a knee injury while celebrating a sack of the New England Patriots' Drake Maye. Hutchinson jumped in jubilation, and when he landed, his right knee buckled.

He immediately crumpled to the ground in pain.

Details of the injury weren't immediately clear. But the initial reports aren't good. Hutchinson might be out for the season. If so, it will mark the second season-ending injury of his five-season NFL career.

The injury to a critical player isn't just a significant and self-inflicted blow to a Lions team that's hoping to compete for the Super Bowl. It also puts Hutchinson in the ranks of the most infamous celebration-induced injuries in NFL history.

Painful memories of Stephon Tulloch in Detroit

For Lions fans, Hutchinson's injury hit too close to home.

In 2014, linebacker Stephon Tulloch celebrated after a stop against Aaron Rodgers and the Green Bay Packers. Like Hutchinson, Tulloch took a celebratory leap in response to the play.

When he landed, he fell to the turf, mid hip-thrust in mockery of Rodgers' corporate-sponsored discount double-check celebration that was very much in vogue in the moment.

The result of the celebration was a torn ACL and the end of Tulloch's season three games in.

For the record, Tulloch said of the injury-inducing celebration : "I'd do it again, brother."

Bill Gramatica tears ACL celebrating first-quarter FG

For the broader NFL fan base of a certain age, Bill Gramatica's injury was likely the first to come to mind.

Gramatica played parts of four NFL seasons as a kicker for the Dolphins and Cardinals. As a rookie, he — like Hutchinson and Tulloch since — jumped in jubilation to celebrate a play in Week 13 of the 2001 season. The result was an injury that would have been instantly memeable had social media been a thing.

When landing from his jubilant jump, Gramatica landed awkwardly on his plant leg and tore the ACL in his right knee.

Making Gramatica's injury even more infamous was the situation of his kick. Gramatica was celebrating a 42-yard yard field goal that broke a scoreless first-quarter tie in a regular-season game against the Giants for a five-win Cardinals team.

The kick was ultimately meaningless in a game the Giants won. The ensuing celebration cost the Cardinals their starting kicker for the rest of the season. To his credit, Gramatica was able to laugh about it years after the fact.

And he offered some public words of encouragement on Sunday in an interview with ESPN, whom he told that he received texts that he was trending on social media.

"For some reason, people tend to remember me every time something like that happens," Gramatica told ESPN . "This is the most high-profile one I think we've seen. "It's going to sting for a while, but it won't define him. He's such an incredible athlete, and he's going to come back. He's already playing with a chip on his shoulder, it feels like. So this is just going to add to that."

"For some reason, people tend to remember me every time something like that happens," Gramatica told ESPN . "This is the most high-profile one I think we've seen.

"It's going to sting for a while, but it won't define him. He's such an incredible athlete, and he's going to come back. He's already playing with a chip on his shoulder, it feels like. So this is just going to add to that."

Lamarr Houston's discount double-check ACL tear

Rodgers, as expected, was a popular target of derision from NFC North rivals — even when he wasn't involved in a game.

This was the case during a 2014 Week 8 matchup between the Chicago Bears and New England Patriots. With the Patriots holding a 48-23 fourth-quarter lead, Bears pass rusher Lamarr Houston secured a meaningless sack.

It wasn't even a sack of Tom Brady. Jimmy Garoppolo had subbed in for garbage time.

Like Tulloch weeks before him, Houston leapt into the air and landed in discount double-check formation. Also like Tulloch, he sustained a torn ACL.

The CBS broadcast took notice immediately with a reference to Tulloch's torn ACL in Week 3 of the same season.

Gus Frerotte's place in injury infamy is unlike the plays above. But in the annals of absurd self-inflicted on-field injuries, this one is the most absurd.

The then-Washington quarterback didn't experience a bad landing after jumping to celebrate a play. Instead, he ran head-first into a wall with the crown of his helmet.

This took place during a Week 12 home game in 1997 against the New York Giants. Frerotte rolled right from the 1-yard line to score a go-ahead touchdown in the second quarter that broke a scoreless tie.

He kept running through the end zone and fired the ball into the padded wall at what was then known as Jack Kent Cooke Stadium. He then lowered his head and plowed it directly into the wall, apparently confident that the thin padding would protect him from injury.

It did not. The result for Frerotte was a sprained neck and a trip to the hospital. Backup Jeff Hostetler finished the game for Washington against his former Giants, and the game ended in a 7-7 tie.

Frerotte returned the next week only for his season to end against the Rams with a broken hip. He went on to play 11 more seasons of a 15-season NFL career that featured 93 starts. His self-inflicted neck injury was the hallmark moment of his playing days.

"You know, if you didn't have a sense of humor about it, I don't think that you would ever survive it," Frerotte said in 2017, per NFL Network . "Because I don't think I go anywhere without somebody talking about it, or asking me about it, or what happened.

"And they try to be nice, but they really kind of want to be mean — some people. And other people just want to know what happened."

articles.title: Raiders' Fernando Mendoza Says 'It's Good to Get Punched in the Face' After Losing 1st NFL Start
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza hadn't lost a game that he started in almost two years, but that streak came to an end in his first NFL start on Sunday.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza hadn't lost a game that he started in almost two years, but that streak came to an end in his first NFL start on Sunday.

The top pick in the 2026 NFL draft struggled in a loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, but he recognizes that the rough first start is a part of the learning process.

"It's good to get punched in the face because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn," he said after the game, per ESPN's Ryan McFadden .

Mendoza, who had appeared in just one NFL game so far, threw for just 143 yards on 17-of-29 passing, though he also added 22 yards on the ground and found the end zone with his legs for his first career score.

Mendoza clearly had some trouble adjusting to the speed of the NFL, as he was sacked six times for a total loss of 45 yards.

"He was playing chess and he fooled me a couple times," Mendoza said of Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald.

Despite a less-than-ideal stat line from Mendoza, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak praised his quarterback after his first start.

"He was well prepared. He started the game really well," Kubiak said. "Overall, for his first start, I thought it was a good start."

Still, Kubiak agreed there's room to grow for both Mendoza and the rest of the team.

"You can learn a lot from every part of this game," Kubiak said. "Overall, we gotta play better. We gotta support him better. I gotta help him better in the second half."

The Raiders drafted Mendoza first overall in April but also brought in veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins over the offseason. Cousins was the starter at the start of the year, giving Mendoza the chance to learn behind him.

But plans changed last week after Las Vegas traded Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings, thrusting Mendoza into the starting role.

Things didn't go that well on Sunday, but he has the rest of the season to continue growing into the franchise player the Raiders hope he can be.

articles.title: 49ers Beat Cowboys, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Keenan Allen, CMC, Dak, Purdy, Pickens, More
articles.summary: Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey and the San Francisco 49ers stormed into Texas and walked away with a 46-40 win over Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday.
articles.body:
Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey and the San Francisco 49ers stormed into Texas and walked away with a 46-40 win over Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday.

The 49ers entered the matchup as 4.5-point favorites over the Cowboys, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

San Francisco held off Dallas' fourth-quarter comeback attempts to secure the win, led by three touchdowns from McCaffrey and two from Deebo Samuel Sr.

The 49ers remain atop the NFC West, improving to 8-1, while the Cowboys fell to 4-6 in the NFC East.

It was a high-scoring first half, with San Francisco holding a 17-16 lead over Dallas at the break.

Purdy found Samuel Sr. for a touchdown in the first quarter before connecting with McCaffrey on a short pass that the running back turned into a 74-yard touchdown.

On the other end, Prescott connected with George Pickens for a 35-yard touchdown pass in the first quarter before finding him for another score in the second.

An interception late in the third quarter proved costly for the Cowboys after the 49ers found the end zone on both of their possessions in the period. Kaelon Black rushed for a touchdown before Samuel Sr. broke loose for a 70-yard rushing score to lead 31-19.

Despite the Cowboys cutting the deficit to six points in the fourth quarter on Pickens' third receiving touchdown of the day and Ryan Flournoy's first, Dallas' defense struggled to stop Purdy and the 49ers' offense.

San Francisco added two more scores in the fourth quarter, with McCaffrey rushing for a touchdown before hauling in a 66-yard touchdown reception to record his third score of the day.

CeeDee Lamb scored his first touchdown of the day as the clock wound down, cutting the deficit to six points.

Dallas then attempted an onside kick, but the 49ers recovered and held off a potential game-winning Hail Mary drive from the Cowboys to secure the win.

The Cowboys will host the Tennessee Titans next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET, while the 49ers will host the Minnesota Vikings at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Seahawks receiver Tory Horton made one of the smartest plays you'll ever see in Seattle's win over Las Vegas
articles.summary: Tory Horton's brilliant kickoff swat burned critical seconds off the clock and triggered the two-minute warning in the Seattle Seahawks' win.
articles.body: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is a Super Bowl champion for a reason. He's a damn good football coach. Perhaps nothing showed how well Seattle is coached quite like a play Seahawks receiver Tory Horton made in the final minutes. With the Seahawks leading 21-10, Matt Gay kicked a 43-yard field goal to make it a one-score game. The Raiders had 2:04 on the clock and two timeouts left as they lined up for the ensuing kickoff, leaving them with a decision. They could attempt an onside kick or just kick it deep and play defense. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Las Vegas elected to kick it deep, but that brought another problem into play. If the Seahawks could burn at least four seconds off the clock during the kick return, it would take the game to the two-minute warning and eliminate one of the remaining clock stoppages. So, the Raiders had two choices: kick the ball out of the back of the end zone or deliberately kick the ball out of bounds along the sideline. If the Raiders weren’t sure Gay could get it out the back, I think they should’ve kicked it out of bounds and lived with giving Seattle the ball at the 40. A touchback would’ve put Seattle at the 35. Gay elected the former and booted the ball as far as he could. His kick sailed into the air and appeared headed out of the end zone. But that's when Horton made one of the smartest football plays I think I've ever seen. HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME ENDS WITH THREE LATERALS, A FOOLED DEFENSE & THE HIGHEST IQ PLAY YOU'LL EVER SEE The Seahawks wide receiver leapt and swatted the kick before it could sail out the back of the end zone. Once the ball hit the ground, Horton immediately started pointing at teammate Rashid Shaheed, as if to say, "pick it up and run!" Shaheed did exactly that, scooping up the ball in the end zone and returning it to the Seahawks’ 19-yard line. But, more importantly, he ran five seconds off the clock and brought the game to the two-minute warning. Macdonald came onto the field with a huge smile, celebrating and congratulating Horton for making the heads-up play. WATCH: After the play, officials huddled and spoke with Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak. According to the official gamebook, they flagged Horton for an illegal bat, and Las Vegas declined the penalty. CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore said he didn’t think Horton’s play was illegal. The rulebook backs him up. Rule 12-5-1(b) prohibits batting a loose ball in the end zone after it has touched the ground. Horton swatted the kick before it ever hit the turf. Seattle took over at its own 19 with 1:59 left. If Las Vegas had used both remaining timeouts on the first two downs and then stopped Seattle inbounds on third down, the Seahawks could have burned up to 40 seconds before punting. Drew Lock made that moot when he ran for 15 yards on second-and-11. He took three knees from there to finish off a 21-13 win. articles.title: Cowboys' Schottenheimer Slams 'Unacceptable' Defense, Jerry Jones Reacts to Historic Loss vs. 49ers
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys' defense has been a huge issue, yet again, during the 2026 season. Those issues were on full display Sunday as the San Francisco 49ers carved them to shreds in a 46-40 win.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys' defense has been a huge issue, yet again, during the 2026 season. Those issues were on full display Sunday as the San Francisco 49ers carved them to shreds in a 46-40 win.

That included giving up 29 points in the second half alone, including two scoring plays of 66 yards or more.

After the contest, head coach Brian Schottenheimer didn't mince words about the second-half effort.

"I thought it was unacceptable," he told reporters . "The tackling was atrocious."

"At the end of the day, we tackled like s--t in the second half," he added .

It was bad. Really, really bad. The Cowboys gave up a whopping 584 yards of total offense to San Francisco, didn't register a single turnover and allowed the Niners to convert 6-of-11 third-down attempts.

And while the Cowboys aren't always this bad on defense, those woes in general have become a definitive pattern.

Nonetheless, team owner and de facto general manager Jerry Jones continued to defend first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker following the loss.

But if the Cowboys (4-6) hope to catch the New York Giants (5-3-1) and emerge on top of a very winnable NFC East this season, the defense is going to need to play better. Even a mediocre defense might be enough to save the season.

But the Cowboys are far below mediocre on that side of the ball at this point.

articles.title: 5 momentous plays in Week 10: Aidan Hutchinson's fateful celebration, Kirk Cousins' timely sack shift power in NFC North
articles.summary: There's often a quirky element to game-deciding plays, but Week 10 seemed to take it to a very strange level, including a broken play that turned a potential...
articles.body:
This week's momentous plays included an injury on a celebration and a sack that actually helped the offense. That these two plays from separate games were connected via the tight NFC North race made them all the more weighty.

There's often a quirky element to game-deciding plays, but Week 10 seemed to take it to a very strange level, including a broken play that turned a potential punt into a 71-yard touchdown.

We also had another notable injury make the list, but for good measure, we finished this top-five off with a good, old-fashioned highlight-reel catch.

Here are this week's most momentous plays from the league's early games in Week 10.

One of the biggest losses happened in one of the largest victories of Week 10.

The Lions cruised to a 35-10 victory over the Patriots in Munich , and Aidan Hutchinson had a sack on the Patriots' opening drive, but it ended horribly. Hutchinson celebrated the sack of Drake Maye and came down awkwardly on his leg, falling to the ground.

The early reports are grim, suggesting Hutchinson might be done for the season. What a massive blow for a Lions defense that had made some real, tangible progress the past five games, holding each of their opponents to 21 or fewer points.

The Lions' victory kept them nominally in the tight NFC North race, sitting at 7-2 overall, but Hutchinson's injury threatens to undermine their chances of making the playoffs. It was a tough game for the Patriots, getting blown out and losing Drake Maye and A.J. Brown to injuries, but the Lions might have had more at stake.

There were several big momentum turns in the Minnesota-Green Bay game, mostly in the Vikings' favor, including a fumble recovery on the Packers' second offensive play on Sunday. But one massive sequence in the second quarter seemed to tilt the game dramatically in Minnesota's corner.

The Vikings were driving, trying to build on their 10-0 lead with the their defense dominating to that point. On a second-and-10 play from the Green Bay 20-yard line, Kirk Cousins appeared to throw an ill-timed interception in his first game back with the Vikings.

Cousins was more than happy to take the sack in that spot. His knee clearly was down as he was awkwardly trying to get rid of the ball, so the Vikings got a reprieve.

On third-and-15, Cousins made arguably his prettiest pass of the day, dropping in a beautiful ball for 24 yards to Tai Felton, setting Minnesota up at the 1-yard line. Aaron Jones would punch it in one play after that for a 17-0 Vikings lead and a stunned Lambeau Field.

The Packers lost a fumble on a wildly off-target shotgun snap, leading to another Vikings field goal, and they'd cough up a chance to make it a one-score game in the second half with a fumble on a kickoff return. It was that kind of day for the Packers, but they dug too big of a first-half hole to climb back and lost 30-10 .

Drew Lock did his job replacing an injured Sam Darnold in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders , and he did it his way. Lock's first touchdown pass of the game was a wild, swashbuckling play, hitting Cooper Kupp for a highlight score.

But Lock's second TD pass might have tilted the game in Seattle's favor — and he was lucky to have put the ball in a perfect spot.

The Seahawks were facing a third-and-3 from their own 29-yard line, nursing a 14-10 lead in the third quarter. Lock dropped back and appeared to have a wide-open Rashid Shaheed for a first-down chain mover. But Lock was dialed in on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who stumbled a bit at the top of his route. That forced Lock to double-clutch and roll out to his left.

When Lock bought time, JSN regained his footing and turned on the jets. Lock threw a perfectly placed deep ball, and Smith-Njigba did the rest.

The Seahawks took back momentum in the game before that, but it was on a knife's edge. Had they failed to get the first down, they're punting to the Raiders in a one-score game. This touchdown provided the cushion the Seahawks needed.

The Jets' chances of beating the Bills got dented when Geno Smith took a big hit just before halftime.

Smith was high-lowed by Buffalo's Terrel Bernard and TJ Parker on the Jets' final offensive play of the first half. He went to the medical tent to be evaluated for a concussion.

The Jets kicked a field goal with 12 seconds left in the second quarter, cutting the Bills' lead to 10-6. Smith missed the start of the second half, and rookie backup Cade Klubnik led the Jets on a field-goal drive in his NFL debut, making it a 10-9 game.

Smith later cleared protocol, returning briefly, but he left again with an ankle injury. The Jets' offense never found a rhythm, kicking one more field goal while Buffalo extended its lead to blowout territory in its 31-12 victory . Smith's injuries let Buffalo pull away after a tighter first half.

The Texans were doing whatever they wanted early on in Cleveland, storming out to a 17-0 lead as C.J. Stroud was on fire to start the game. The Browns started shifting the tide in the second quarter.

After a much-needed field goal and (finally!) a stop on defense, Deshaun Watson took a deep shot late in the second quarter. Watson had great time and found Jerry Jeudy for a 65-yard bomb down to the Houston 6-yard line.

Jeudy stumbled but hauled it in, setting up Watson's 6-yard keeper for a massive touchdown. That made it a 17-10 game with just over four minutes left in the first half and turned a potential blowout into a one-score game. The Browns finished off the first half strong with an interception of Stroud, and they dominated the third quarter, eventually taking a 20-17 lead and holding on for a 27-24 victory .

Jeudy is sometimes forgotten, but he's made a few clutch catches downfield this season, including a 33-yard grab against the Ravens in Week 6 on the late comeback drive and a 30-yarder against the Saints in Week 9 that helped set up a game-tying field goal. Sunday's catch was as big or bigger than either one.

articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones put together another rough outing in Sunday's win against the Miami Dolphins, but his status as the starter won't change.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones put together another rough outing in Sunday's win against the Miami Dolphins, but his status as the starter won't change.

Colts head coach Shane Steichen said that the team will stick with Jones under center for Thursday's contest against the Houston Texans.

"We're on a short week, so we've got to go," Steichen said, per ESPN's Stephen Holder .

Jones threw for just 108 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while completing 11 of 22 pass attempts in a 24-22 win over the Dolphins. It marked his fourth consecutive game with 180 passing yards or fewer.

Should the Colts eventually move Jones to the bench, it would presumably be Anthony Richardson under center. Richardson hasn't started a game or played significant snaps in a game since the 2024 season.

Second-year quarterback Riley Leonard is also available for the Colts.

Indianapolis opted not to trade Jones at the deadline despite reported interest from a handful of teams. Keeping him on the roster perhaps indicates that the Colts still have some faith that he can return to the 2025 version of himself who was putting up career numbers before a season-ending torn Achilles.

Indianapolis' playoff hopes are virtually over at 3-7, so now is the time to experiment with the roster before making big decisions this offseason. For now, it'll remain Jones' starting job to lose.

articles.title: 'Genius' batted ball on kick return helps Seahawks burn clock, sparks officiating confusion in win over Raiders
articles.summary: A bizarre play helped the Seahawks run out the clock in their 21-13 win over the Raiders Sunday. It also sparked officiating confusion that remained unsettle...
articles.body:
A bizarre play that the CBS broadcast hailed as "genius" and drew a pat on the back from head coach Mike Macdonald helped the Seattle Seahawks run out the clock on their 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.

It also sparked officiating confusion that remained unsettled postgame.

The play in question took place on a Las Vegas kickoff with 2:04 remaining and Seattle holding a 21-13 lead. Matt Gay's kick appeared destined to go out of the end zone for a touchback with no time taken off the clock that would have given Seattle the ball at the 35-yard line.

But Tory Horton had different ideas. The Seahawks return man leapt and batted the ball toward the field of play before it could sail out of bounds. He then instructed Rashid Shaheed to pick it up and return it. Shaheed obliged, and when he was tackled at the 19-yard line, the game clock had run down to 1:59, inside the 2-minute warning.

When the play was done, Macdonald greeted Horton with a smile, a high-five and a pat on the back.

Horton's decision to keep the ball in play cost Seattle 16 yards. More importantly, it eliminated the 2-minute warning from Seattle's ensuing offensive possession. It essentially robbed the Raiders of a valuable de facto timeout.

The Seahawks went on to get a first down and kneel out the clock on the win in victory formation. Even if they hadn't managed a first down, Las Vegas, which had two timeouts remaining, wouldn't have been able to get the ball back with any substantial time on the clock thanks to Horton's play. His decision and Shaheed's execution essentially eliminated 40 seconds of game clock.

After the game, Horton discussed his decision with reporters and what was discussed with coaches prior to to the kick.

"All he said was keep the ball in play, field every return, just don't let it go out," Horton said, apparently referring to special teams coach Jay Harbaugh. "Make sure we don't kneel it in the end zone."

From there, the situational awareness and decision-making was all on Horton.

"I took into consideration, I'm gonna try by any means keep this ball in play so we can get a return started. … I made sure I knew where I was on the field before I leaped up, made sure I was in bounds taking off.

"It's just the situational awareness of like knowing the distance and the time and the situation of the game of knowing, all right, this is a must return. .. I just wanted to make sure I made the smartest play for us."

The legality of the play wasn't immediately clear. Officials conferred at the play's conclusion and held a lengthy discussion before addressing the crowd.

After meeting with the Raiders' sideline, referee Bill Vinovich offered this explanation that didn't exactly provide clarity:

CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore was left perplexed after watching the ordeal and didn't agree that a penalty had actually occurred.

"It sounds to me like Bill is saying that there was maybe a foul," Steratore said. "I don't think it's a foul. It's a kick that never hits the ground. I believe you can bat a kick in the air, provided it has never hit the ground yet."

Per the game's official play-by-play , the play was, indeed, ruled an "illegal bat." And the Raiders declined the penalty, since accepting it wouldn't have put time back on the clock.

Here's the definition of an illegal bat, per section 12-5-1 of the NFL rulebook:

Article 1. Illegal Bat It is an illegal bat if: any player bats or punches a loose ball in the field of play toward his opponent's goal line; any player bats or punches a loose ball (that has touched the ground) in any direction, if it is in either end zone; an offensive player bats a backward pass in flight toward his opponent's goal line a forward pass that is controlled by a player prior to completing the catch is thrown forward (the ball remains alive if caught by a teammate or intercepted). Exception: A forward pass in flight may be tipped, batted, or deflected in any direction by any eligible player at any time.

any player bats or punches a loose ball in the field of play toward his opponent's goal line;

any player bats or punches a loose ball (that has touched the ground) in any direction, if it is in either end zone;

an offensive player bats a backward pass in flight toward his opponent's goal line

a forward pass that is controlled by a player prior to completing the catch is thrown forward (the ball remains alive if caught by a teammate or intercepted).

Exception: A forward pass in flight may be tipped, batted, or deflected in any direction by any eligible player at any time.

Is the ball in the "field of play" when it's sailing out of bound without having touched the ground on a kickoff? If so, the bat would appear to be illegal per subsection 1 above. If not, officials got it wrong.

Steratore appeared to have referenced subsection 2, which declares the bat of a ball "in either end zone" illegal when the ball "has touched the ground." The ball hadn't touched the ground, so this would not apply to Horton's play in determining that the bat was illegal.

The rulebook defines the "field of play" as "the area bounded by goal lines and sidelines." It goes on to define the end zones separately as "the areas bounded by goal lines, end lines, and sidelines." This appears to add up to Horton's play having legally taken place outside the "field of play" and officials getting it wrong.

Even if the Raiders had accepted the penalty, time wasn't going to be put back on the clock. The goal of pushing the clock under the 2-minute warning was accomplished, and it turned out to be a heads-up play by Horton that few if anybody watching Sunday had seen before — legal or not.

articles.summary: There was no stopping Joe Burrow in the first half of Sunday night's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
There was no stopping Joe Burrow in the first half of Sunday night's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback threw for 302 yards and three touchdowns as he helped his team take a 24-3 lead into halftime.

The dominant first half has NFL fans ready to declare him MVP.

Burrow was already the favorite to win MVP coming into the night with +125 odds on FanDuel Sportsbook , and his odds will likely only get better after his outstanding showing against the Steelers.

Just behind Burrow are Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (+320), San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (+410) and Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (+450). All four have had great seasons, but it's hard to argue for anyone other than Burrow at this point.

He came into Week 10 with the second-most passing yards (2,386) and the most touchdowns (23). The Bengals are 6-2 and are heading toward 7-2 after the fast start on Sunday.

Burrow played like an MVP in 2024, but ultimately didn't win the award because of a rough season for his team. Last year, he played just eight games while dealing with injuries.

Now, Burrow could finally take home the most coveted individual award in football.

articles.title: Two games, one day: Ground stop means unprecedented double duty for NFL refs
articles.summary: It was 4:17 p.m. Sunday in downtown Indianapolis when the Colts wrapped up a home win over the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body: It was 4:17 p.m. Sunday in downtown Indianapolis when the Colts wrapped up a home win over the Miami Dolphins. Fans departed Lucas Oil Stadium. The teams scattered for home. For the four-man officiating crew that worked the game, the work day was only half over. The quartet boarded a van 24 minutes later and drove east for Cincinnati, where their second assignment of the day awaited — an unusual case of double duty that was set in motion by the FAA ground stop Friday that halted flights nationwide. Holding an electrolyte drink and a portable massage gun, referee Don Willard arrived inside Cincinnati’s Paycor Stadium at 6:37 p.m., about 90 minutes before the Bengals hosted the Pittsburgh Steelers, along with his crew of umpire Terry Killens, field judge Jabir Walker and side judge Justin Larrew. “To best of our knowledge, no NFL official has worked two games in one day,” the NFL Referees Association told NBC News in a statement. “Officials have worked two games in a week before, but we can’t find an instance where one has worked a double header like this.” Friday’s four-hour ground stop did not require the NFL to adjust the kickoff times of any of Sunday’s games because air travel resumed by Saturday, when road teams traditionally travel. The teams would arrive on time; to ensure the referees would, too, the NFL reassigned officials to games within driving distance of where they live. In an extreme case, referee Clete Blakeman — who was supposed to officiate the game in Cincinnati — drove about eight hours from his home in Nebraska to Green Bay to work the Packers-Vikings game, ESPN reported. “We appreciate the commitment and dedication of all the officials, numerous gameday personnel and our network partners who made adjustments due to nationwide travel issues,” an NFL spokesperson said. Seventeen officiating crews work in the NFL, and each has a backup referee who trains throughout the year to step in if necessary, the spokesman said. Three of those backup referees were pressed into duty Sunday. One was Willard, who has typically been a side judge during his nine years in the NFL. Sunday marked both his debut as a referee (Colts-Dolphins) — and his second career game as a referee. Willard had done a “phenomenal job,” longtime NFL officials and NBC Sports rules analyst Terry McAuley said during NBC’s “Sunday Night Football” broadcast. Officials are paid per game worked, the referee union said. “This is a unique and unprecedented situation that has required all of our officials to make adjustments, and in some cases, travel many miles by car to get to their game sites,” said Scott Green, the executive director of the NFLRA. “However, over the course of their careers, all officials have faced unpublicized travel and other assorted issues, meaning they have experience working in less- than-ideal situations, in many games across all levels of play. Our members will do what they have always done, which is work the games to the best of their ability, regardless of the situation.”

articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson tore it up on Sunday, catching nine passes for 74 yards on 13 targets during a 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers.

As you might imagine, he was quite happy to be reunited with quarterback Kirk Cousins, who rejoined the team this week after being traded from the Las Vegas Raiders.

Vikings Dominate Packers in Kirk's Return

"It felt great. Honestly, it just felt great," Jefferson told NFL Network's Stacey Dales. "Off of a short week with [Cousins], coming to our team with no expectations, for real. For him to come here and have a composed mind—came in here and just dialed it up. Didn't really force anything. Of course we've gotta limit the turnovers, but all in all he had a great game."

Cousins finished the game with 207 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. He was immediately a massive upgrade over Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, providing the Vikings with the quality quarterback play they've been solely lacking. And just as importantly, Cousins made it a priority to target Jefferson early and often.

At 7-2, Minnesota finds itself in a three-way tie atop the NFC North with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears. Green Bay isn't far behind at 6-4. The margin for error in the division is razor thin.

But the Cousins-Jefferson duo, alongside the team's fantastic defense, certainly gives them a shot to be a real contender.

articles.title: Cowboys' Dak Prescott Says 49ers Fans 'Were More Present Than Ours' After Loss at AT&T Stadium
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys had a home game against the San Francisco 49ers, but it might have felt more like a road game.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys had a home game against the San Francisco 49ers, but it might have felt more like a road game.

Niners fans flocked to AT&T Stadium, and Dak Prescott said their presence was felt when asked if the Cowboys had to use a silent count.

"No, we didn't go on the silent count," Prescott told reporters . "[We] anticipated it. I think y'all even potentially asked me on Thursday about it, having this many 49er fans there. Tricked myself and told myself early on that the red was for my high school.

"And at the end of the day, all I asked for is a great environment to play this game. And unfortunately, their fans were more present than ours, but it created a great atmosphere. So, we take the good out of it one way or another."

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he wasn't that surprised to see so many 49ers fans.

"Well, they always have a lot of fans here, and they travel really good. We have a lot of them on the road ourselves, Cowboys fans," Jones said, per Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News. "So it was not unexpected at all. We knew how many tickets that they were buying as we led up to this particular game, I've known that for weeks and weeks. This was a big game."

Prescott put together a tremendous performance on Sunday as the Cowboys faced the 49ers, but it wasn't enough in a 46-40 loss.

"I do truly believe that we have the people, but something's gotta change," Prescott said.

Prescott couldn't have done much more to keep Dallas in the game as he threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns. His only major mistake was an interception that led to a touchdown, but he made up for it with a touchdown on the following drive.

But five touchdowns couldn't make up for a historically bad day on defense.

There's no question that the Cowboys' defense needs to improve for them to make the playoffs, but whether they can make a big enough change before it's too late remains to be seen.

"I'm not gonna say it's slipping away," Prescott said. "We're putting ourselves in a bind. We're making it really, really hard on ourselves, and we're the only ones who can change it to fix it."

articles.title: Cuba conquista la NFL: Fernando Mendoza debuta como quarterback titular de los Raiders
articles.summary: Los campeones Seattle Seahawks derrotaron por 13-21 a Las Vegas Raiders, que tuvieron la titularidad de Fernando Mendoza, 'quarterback' de origen cubano, en partido de la semana 10 de la temporada de la NFL.
articles.body: Los campeones Seattle Seahawks derrotaron por 13-21 a Las Vegas Raiders, que tuvieron la titularidad de Fernando Mendoza, 'quarterback' de origen cubano, en partido de la semana 10 de la temporada de la NFL. El joven de 23 años pasó para 143 yardas, completó 17 de 29 envíos, y logró una anotación por tierra; no fue interceptado, aunque sufrió seis capturas de la agresiva línea de los Seahawks. Aunque Mendoza ya había debutado con los plata y negro el pasado 11 de octubre, en sustitución de Kirk Cousins, en el último cuarto del juego ante los New England Patriots, hoy tuvo su primer inicio. Con Seattle, Drew Look pasó para 240 yardas y tuvo dos conexiones a las diagonales. La victoria colocó a los Seahawks con seis ganados y cuatro perdidos en el segundo puesto de la división Oeste de la Conferencia Nacional (NFC). También este domingo los San Francisco 49ers confirmaron su condición de favoritos en la NFC con su triunfo 40-46 sobre los Dallas Cowboys en un emocionante juego. Los Cowboys cayeron a pesar del buen desempeño de Dak Prescott, quien acumuló 343 yardas y cinco envíos a las diagonales; fue interceptado en una ocasión. Además de los tres envíos a las diagonales, Stafford sumó 249 yardas; fue interceptado una vez y capturado dos veces. También lució en la ofensiva de los Rams, Blake Corum, quien corrió para 100 yardas y tuvo un viaje a las diagonales. Por los Cardinals, Carson Beck acumuló 108 yardas, dos intercepciones y fue capturado en cinco ocasiones. Los Rams quedaron con marca de 6-4, empatados con los Seahawks en el Oeste de la NFC, que lideran los 49ers; los Cardinals tienen récord de 3-7 en la misma división. articles.title: Joe Burrow makes MVP statement and Bengals destroy Steelers in blowout win
articles.summary: Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase were on fire for the Bengals on Sunday night.
articles.body: Joe Burrow is looking more and more like the NFL's MVP this season. And on Sunday night, the Cincinnati Bengals looked like a real threat to win a Super Bowl. The Bengals' dismantling of the Pittsburgh Steelers seemed like a possible dawning of something special for Cincinnati. The Bengals were that good in a 38-18 win against the Steelers, who were 6-2 coming in. The Bengals are 7-2 and now have the lead spot in the AFC North race. Burrow was nearly perfect, the Bengals' offensive line stymied the Steelers' pass rush and Cincinnati's defense shut down Pittsburgh. Burrow had 409 passing yards and four touchdowns, and could have had much more if the Steelers kept the game competitive. Ja'Marr Chase also lit it up with 11 catches for 231 yards. Burrow had at least four total touchdowns for the fifth straight game, tying an NFL record set by Peyton Manning in 2004, according to NBC. Burrow is on pace for more than 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns this season. The Bengals have accepted a pass-heavy approach and Burrow is executing at a very high level. It was a statement in the AFC North race. But after the way the Bengals played Sunday night in all phases, winning a division should be just the first part of Cincinnati's vision board. The team that a big national television audience watched Sunday night is capable of making a deep playoff run and maybe even finally winning it all. Cincinnati has stunning first halfThe Bengals' mauling of the Steelers was unbelievable. It was the kind of domination you see in college, not the NFL. When the Bengals took a 17-0 lead with 5:28 left in the second quarter, some of the stats were hard to believe. Burrow was 21-of-26 passing for 245 yards at that point, and Aaron Rodgers was 0-for-7. It was the longest streak without a completion to start a game in Rodgers' 22-year career. He'd be 0-for-8 before completing his first pass. Chase had 135 receiving yards at that point. The Steelers as a team had 14. The Bengals had 18 first downs while the Steelers had one.At halftime, Burrow had 302 yards and three touchdowns. He hit Dohnte Meyers for a 15-yard touchdown with nine seconds left in the half to give the Bengals a 24-3 lead. The Steelers were outgained 337-40 in the first half. It is very hard to beat a professional team that thoroughly. Sometimes it can happen against an overmatched team or one that is heavily injured at the end of a lost season. This was a Steelers team that was tied for first place in the division coming in and was reasonably healthy. It was arguably the best half of football any NFL team has played all season. Bengals' defense shines tooThe Bengals' offense is very good and has been for some time. The defense is still working to get respect, and that might have been the most promising part of a fantastic win against the Steelers. The Bengals made Rodgers look like a quarterback who will turn 43 years old next month. He missed on several throws and was harassed by the Bengals' pass rush most of the night. When the game was still up for grabs, the Steelers couldn't even run the ball against a defense that had been vulnerable against good rushing attacks. Nothing within Pittsburgh's offense worked. Through three quarters the Steelers averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per play. That's probably a bad sign for Pittsburgh going forward, but also improvement from Cincinnati after it gave up 411 yards and 30 points to the Steelers in a Week 3 loss. Since the Bengals came up just short of beating the Rams in Super Bowl LVI, the franchise seemed to be taking steps back. The Bengals missed the playoffs altogether each of the past three seasons. Their offensive line has regularly struggled to protect Burrow and the defense sunk near the bottom of the NFL. Those areas have been cleaned up this season, through investments on the offensive line in the draft and free agency and a big addition on defense with an aggressive offseason trade to get defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II. The top of the AFC is tough this season. But an MVP-level quarterback with two superstar receivers, a solid offensive line and a much improved defense gives the Bengals a shot at doing something special. If they play in January like they did Sunday night, they'll be tough to beat.

articles.title: Joe Burrow Helps Bengals Dominate Steelers, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Rodgers, Chase, More
articles.summary: Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals defeated Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers, 38-18, in an AFC North showdown on Sunday night.
articles.body:
Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals defeated Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers, 38-18, in an AFC North showdown on Sunday night.

The Bengals entered the matchup as 3.5-point home favorites over the Steelers, per FanDuel Sportsbook , securing the win by 20 points behind a four touchdown performance from Burrow.

Ja'Marr Chase also had an explosive game for Cincinnati, hauling in 11 receptions for 231 yards. He moved into first place for the most games with at least 10 receptions by a player in his first six NFL seasons.

The victory moved the Bengals into first place in the AFC North, improving to 7-2 overall and 2-1 in division play. The Steelers fell to second place at 6-3 overall and 2-2 in division play.
