3. CLE: 5-4 (OVR), 2-1 (DIV), 3-3 (CONF)

4. BAL: 4-5 (OVR), 0-2 (DIV), 2-4 (CONF)

The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions to take a commanding 24-3 lead into halftime.

Burrow found tight end Drew Sample for a short touchdown before connecting with Chase Brown for another score. Dohnte Meyers added a 15-yard touchdown reception from Burrow as several Bengals got in on the scoring action in the first half.

Burrow threw for 302 yards on 26-of-32 passing with three touchdowns, carrying a hot hand throughout the first half.

The Steelers remained scoreless in the third quarter while Burrow threw his fourth touchdown pass of the game and Brown hauled in his second touchdown to give Cincinnati a 31-3 lead entering the fourth quarter.

The Steelers found the end zone for the first time in the fourth quarter, with Rodgers connecting with DK Metcalf and a two-point conversion before finding Pat Freiermuth for another touchdown.

Cincinnati's Samaje Perine sandwiched a rushing score between the two Pittsburgh touchdowns, but the Steelers' late surge was far too little too late.

Cincinnati will hit the road to face the Washington Commanders next Monday night at 8:15 p.m. ET, while the Steelers will travel to face the Philadelphia Eagles next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: As Kirk Cousins sparks Vikings, Fernando Mendoza reflects on Raiders debut: 'It's good to get punched in the face'
articles.summary: Perhaps Cousins' summation of his day applies to both teams. "There's just so much football ahead," Cousins said, "and this story is going to get written muc...
articles.body:
Facing third-and-23 in the first quarter, Kirk Cousins dropped back.

His offensive line was slowing the Packers' rushers threatening from his left.

Second-year undrafted free-agent receiver Myles Price was crossing the field from his right.

So Cousins wound up and hit Price on a crosser, Price bouncing off Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse and racing the 14 remaining yards to the end zone.

The 38-yard touchdown marked the first touchdown reception of Price's career and the first in Cousins' return to the Vikings after a Tuesday trade from the Las Vegas Raiders made him the first quarterback to start for two different teams in back-to-back weeks, per Fox.

The timing that play required? The poise in the pocket just four days after Cousins had arrived at the Vikings' practice facility wondering what code he needed to input to enter the building?

"That's probably the [touchdown] that you're thinking, 'Is there enough time on task … ?'" head coach Kevin O'Connell said after the Vikings beat the Packers, 30-10 . "We're kind of in a four-by-one look right there. They're dropping somebody in. Myles runs right into the hook area kind of behind there and you've got to get that ball thrown with pretty elite timing and you're really throwing it into a spot with some trust that Myles is going to go get it because inevitably the corner may fall off.

Improving to 7-2, the Vikings showed their first glimpse of what a high-ceiling offense might look like beside one of the best defenses in the league. Brian Flores' unit was the star of the show yet again, sacking Jordan Love eight times and securing four takeaways. The Vikings contained the Packers to 10 points and 220 yards just one week after Green Bay embarrassed the Patriots to the tune of 45 points and 478 yards.

Add in 312 yards and 30 points on offense after the Vikings averaged 266.8 and 18.3 before Cousins' arrival?

"Obviously there's a lot to build off of from this," O'Connell said. But "for one of the first times this year, I thought we played complementary football."

Expect the ceiling only to rise as Cousins acclimates to his reunion with a team that deemed the remainder of his season worth a third-round pick and a $10 million salary hit.

And the Raiders team that parted with Cousins?

Rookie first overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza started off strongly before the No. 1-ranked Seahawks defense stifled the Raiders in the second half of a 21-13 loss . Mendoza spoke to the opportunity the unraveling could provide.

"It's good to get punched in the face, because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game and as a future hopeful leader of this offense …" Mendoza said. "There's a lot of things I need to improve on in that field, and I'm excited to watch the film and get back to work."

After strong Raiders start, Seahawks tilted 'weird game' in their favor

When former Dallas Cowboys head coach Jason Garrett suggested a recipe to onboard Mendoza last week, it seemed ideal but unrealistic.

"Quiet the game down for him, try to get the running game going early, high-percentage throws early, move the quarterback," Garrett said Wednesday on an NBC conference call . "Try to get him to be 5-for-5 [passing] before he even thinks about it to get into the flow of the game."

As an aspiration, that sounded great. But was a Raiders team that ranked among the league's worst in both rushing and defense really going to be able to support a new quarterback that way? How much could the passing game withstand the loss of Cousins, who ranked fifth in passing yards and 11th in passer rating when he left for Minnesota?

Credit Mendoza and Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak's early game plan: Mendoza not only started 5-for-5 against Seattle; he completed seven straight passes before his first incompletion. Las Vegas' early offense was balanced and steady, Mendoza operating from under center and running bootlegs off play action.

During the first half, Las Vegas kept Seattle's defense honest: Mendoza scrambled for a yard on third-and-1 to keep his first drive alive and later for 8 yards on third-and-5 near first quarter's end. And as if in ode to his fourth-and-4 national championship highlight, Mendoza tucked and ran for a 10-yard touchdown to give the Raiders an early 7-0 lead.

"Got to give the Raiders a lot of credit in the first half," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said afterward. "I thought they had a good plan, and they made it challenging for us in the first half. But our guys did a great job adjusting and sticking together and finding a way to win in the end."

The Seahawks' adjustments, paired with the loss of two-time Pro Bowl tight end Brock Bowers to an ankle injury , derailed a promising start.

With the help of defensive-back blitzes that Macdonald said resulted from in-game looks, the Seahawks sacked Mendoza four times in the second half after just two in the first. Seattle's pressure disrupted the timing of Mendoza's passing game and shuttered the Raiders' run game: After converting 7-of-10 third-down attempts in the first half, Las Vegas went 0-for-7 in the second half. The Raiders followed up a 62-yard rushing performance in the first half with just 3 net yards in the second. Ten first downs in the first half preceded just two across quarters three and four.

And after Mendoza opened the game 11-of-13 for 90 yards passing, in addition to notching the rushing touchdown, before halftime — he managed to complete just 6-of-16 attempts for 53 yards and no touchdowns in the second half.

"It just felt like such a weird game," Raiders tight end Michael Mayer said. "I don't really know how to describe it. Felt like we started out pretty good, and then I really don't know what happened after that."

Kubiak and Mendoza each said they hold themselves to higher standards than they reached in the loss.

"There was a lot of sacks there," Mendoza said. "We should have had half as many if not even less than that. So I need to mature as a quarterback, throw the ball away, throw more accurate balls on third down and making sure we can move the chains to give our defense time to recuperate on the sideline and to really get it going in the second half."

What's next for Cousins' Vikings, Mendoza's Raiders?

The Vikings and Raiders' playoff hopes are trending in different directions.

Minnesota's chances of advancing to the postseason improved to 90% with its Sunday win, per Next Gen Stats, even as it sits in second place in a crowded NFC North . The Raiders' chances fell to 10% after their loss, their 4-6 record paired with their remaining schedule projecting worse chances than also-currently-out-of-it AFC contenders in the New England Patriots, Baltimore Ravens and Houston Texans.

A similarity between the two teams whose fates will be tied this season by their shared Cousins custody: the expectation of evolution as the offensive cast settles into its roles.

In Minnesota, Cousins reunited with a handful of teammates including receiver Justin Jefferson, whom he said "felt like old times watching Justin do what he just did." But plenty of teammates, and parts of the Vikings' playbook like the run concepts assistant head coach Frank Smith implemented this season, remain new. Cousins is no stranger to new play-callers: "I've changed coordinators 11 times," he said after the game. But there were times during his quick turnaround week when Cousins said he told O'Connell and Co., "You know what, I would be more comfortable doing this ."

"You can't just roll the ball out there and ask the quarterback to have all the answers while they're still digesting their in-flight meal from when they came here," O'Connell said.

With just two full-speed practices after Cousins' arrival, O'Connell said he did not think Cousins took a full-speed rep of the double-pump 20-yard touchdown on which he hit Gavin Bartholomew in the fourth quarter.

"I think it was just either a walkthrough or maybe a jog or something, but it looked the way it's supposed to look…" O'Connell said. "Kirk just couldn't have executed better."

Kubiak, meanwhile, was kicking himself for some decisions he implemented with Mendoza. Those rollouts that worked for Mendoza in the first half? "Should have done more of that for sure," Kubiak said of shifting the plan.

The Raiders' resilience to losing Bowers, whose 676 yards and six touchdowns receiving both lead Las Vegas?

"I thought overall when we lost Brock we definitely saw a big change in production," Kubiak said. "So I look at myself. I have to do a much better job of moving the ball and spreading the ball around. …

"Overall, we've got to play better. We've got to support him better."

With just one game down, and a schedule that will lighten in December, the Raiders will have more chances. Perhaps Cousins' summation of his day applies to both teams — as well as to how NFL history will ultimately remember this rare in-season trade of a starting quarterback.

"There's just so much football ahead," Cousins said, "and this story is going to get written much later than now."

Justin Jefferson finished with a game-high nine catches for 77 yards on 13 targets.Minnesota's defense also made its impact felt, as usual, sacking Jordan Love eight times — the most by one team in the NFL this season. Rookie tight end Mark Redman fumbled on the Packers' second offensive play of the game, leading to a Vikings field goal. Will Reichard's third field goal of the game pushed the lead back to 20 points and put the Packers down for good.

articles.body:
Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals are alone in the penthouse of the AFC North at 7-2 after a 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers that came in emphatic fashion . Backup QB Joe Flacco got some burn with the Bengals as Burrow put the Steelers to bed early with an MVP worthy performance.

After the game, Burrow spoke about the significance of squaring off against and beating a player he's loved watching and competing against.

"It is meaningful that we beat the Steelers, I've got a lot of love and respect for Aaron, and I've loved watching him all these years, if this is our last one going against each other, I've just got a lot of respect for him and what he's done."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Burrow had 409 and four touchdowns while Rodgers threw for two second-half scores to make the final tally look more respectable. The AFC North now runs through Cincinnati, and it doesn't look like Burrow and his teammates are going to give up the top spot anytime soon.

Chase Brown and Ja'Marr Chase both starred in the Bengals' win, as did defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence, who danced into the hearts of NFL fans nationwide after a big sack on Rodgers. Brown had 44 yards rushing and 39 yards receiving including two touchdown catches. Chase lit up the secondary of the Steelers with 11 catches for 231 yards, looking like the NFL's best receiver along the way.

The Bengals haven't been to the Super Bowl since 2022, but Burrow and his teammates look like a good bet to make it back after they took control of the AFC North from a player who isn't quite the same as he once was, to say the least.

articles.title: ‘Good to get punched in the face’- Fernando Mendoza embraces harsh lesson from first NFL start
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza has taken a positive lesson from a difficult first NFL start after the Las Vegas Raiders suffered a 21-13 defeat to the Seattle Seahawks. Th...
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza has taken a positive lesson from a difficult first NFL start after the Las Vegas Raiders suffered a 21-13 defeat to the Seattle Seahawks.

The rookie quarterback completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards as the Raiders struggled to find their rhythm against Seattle's defence at Allegiant Stadium.

Mendoza had been waiting for his opportunity to start after weeks of calls from Raiders fans for him to replace Kirk Cousins. However, his first outing also showed how much work lies ahead.

Fernando Mendoza welcomes tough introduction to NFL after Las Vegas Raiders defeat

Rather than dwell on the disappointing result, Mendoza praised the Seahawks' defensive performance and insisted the experience could help him improve.

Speaking after the game, he said: "A lot of credit to them and coach Macdonald…It's good to get punched in the face because now, it's a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game and as a future leader, future hopeful leader of this offense."

It was an honest assessment from the rookie, who will now have plenty to review before the Raiders' next game against the Denver Broncos.

Mendoza's afternoon was made more difficult by the loss of star tight end Brock Bowers to an injury early in the contest. His availability could become an important factor as Las Vegas looks for more production from its passing game.

The numbers also showed the difference between the two offences. Seattle finished with 382 total yards compared with just 163 for the Raiders, while Drew Lock completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards and two touchdowns.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba was particularly difficult to contain, finishing with eight receptions for 171 yards and a touchdown.

Mendoza did manage a 10-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, but Las Vegas could not keep pace after Seattle scored twice in the third.

The Raiders are now 4-6 and face another difficult test against Denver. For Mendoza, the priority will be turning the lessons from his first start into progress as he continues his development in the NFL.

articles.title: Lions Could Add 70-Sack Edge Rusher as Aidan Hutchinson Replacement
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions could sign veteran edge rusher Leonard Floyd to fill the void left after Aidan Hutchinson's injury. The post Lions Could Add 70-Sack Edge R...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions have a gigantic void to fill on defense after edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending injury, but could add a former Super Bowl champion as a bargain replacement.

Hutchinson was hurt early in Sunday's win over the New England Patriots, falling to the turf after leaping in the air while celebrating a sack of quarterback Drake Maye. Hutchinson was ruled out and is feared to have suffered a torn ACL, which would put him out for the season.

Lions Could Grab Former Super Bowl Champion to Fill Defensive Void

The Lions had already suffered another blow when linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a serious injury, and now may need to hit free agency to account for Hutchinson's loss.

While the Lions have yet to make an official statement on Hutchinson's future, the injury is feared to keep him out for the remainder of the season. There are some internal options the team could consider, but there is also at least one veteran who could join the team in free agency.

Bleacher Report's Moe Moton identified 10-year veteran Leonard Floyd as a potential "bargain" addition for a team in need of pass rush help.

"Beset by injuries early in his career, Leonard Floyd didn't miss a game between 2018 and 2024," Moton wrote. "Though Floyd bounced around the league in his prime, he was highly productive after his four-year stint with the Chicago Bears."

Moton noted that Floyd has some very productive seasons in his recent history, along with a Super Bowl season with the Los Angeles Rams.

"Floyd registered at least 8.5 sacks in five consecutive seasons between 2020 and 2024, helping the Los Angeles Rams win Super Bowl LVI over the Cincinnati Bengals with five tackles and a sack," Moton wrote.

Moton suggested that Floyd could still have at least a bit of the athleticism that helped him accumulate 70 career sacks.

"At 34, Floyd may have lost a step that allows him to close on quarterbacks, but he can still move a signal-caller off his spot with pressure off the edge," Moton wrote. "The 10-year pro is best suited as a stopgap defender."

Lions Waiting for Official News on Aidan Hutchinson

Lions head coach Dan Campbell said after Sunday's 35-10 win that the team would need to return to the United States from Germany before they could make a final assessment. But Campbell appeared to hint that it was a significant injury for the team's star edge rusher.

"Any time you lose a player like that and you don't know the entirety of it … it hurts a little bit," Campbell said

articles.title: Browns Urged to Re-Sign Deshaun Watson After 6-4 Start
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson’s comeback against Houston has sparked a push for a new Browns deal. The post Browns Urged to Re-Sign Deshaun Watson After 6-4 Start appeared...
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson's $230 million deal has delivered years of disappointment for the Cleveland Browns, but his latest comeback win has sparked a push to bring him back.

Watson helped Cleveland erase a 17-point deficit in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Houston Texans, moving the Browns to 6-4 heading into their bye. He completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards and led the team with 49 rushing yards and a touchdown.

His sixth fourth-quarter go-ahead drive featured a 30-yard completion to Harold Fannin Jr. that set up Quinshon Judkins' winning touchdown run. After returning to the starting lineup, Watson delivered another reason for Cleveland to keep trusting him.

Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot believes that trust should extend beyond this season.

"Things have been so good with Watson this season, the Browns should re-sign him after the season," Cabot said. "They've been criss-crossing the country watching college quarterbacks all season, and will likely draft one in the first round with one or both of their first-round picks. But the Browns should bring back Watson to build on what he's accomplished this season, and to hit the ground running in 2027."

Browns Could Keep Watson and Still Draft a Quarterback

Cleveland has the resources to pursue its next quarterback without immediately handing him the offense. The Browns hold their own first-round pick and the Rams' selection acquired in the Myles Garrett trade. That gives them flexibility to select a passer or explore moving up for one.

Cabot has previously pointed to Cleveland's extensive scouting as a reason to expect another quarterback investment in the draft . Keeping Watson would give that prospect time to develop while an experienced starter handles the job.

"If sitting awhile is okay for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, it should be good enough for wherever the Browns draft their presumptive quarterback of the future," Cabot said.

Watson would also enter a second season working with Todd Monken, giving Cleveland continuity while the coaching staff prepares a younger quarterback to take over.

Deshaun Watson's Next Contract Could Bring Difficult Negotiations

Agreeing that Watson should return would be only part of the discussion. Determining his price, role and terms could be more complicated. Watson is finishing the five-year, fully guaranteed $230 million deal he signed in 2022. His next agreement would require Cleveland to weigh his late-game success against the inconsistency that still shows up.

He has topped 300 passing yards in three consecutive starts , but has seven touchdown passes against four interceptions this season. Houston intercepted him once and sacked him four times Sunday.

His market elsewhere is another question. Watson's off-field history includes an 11-game suspension in 2022 following sexual misconduct allegations . That history, and the potential blowback of a signing, could complicate another team's willingness to commit to him.

Still, winning gives Watson an argument at the negotiating table. Cleveland is 6-3 in his starts, with each victory requiring him to deliver late.

"I just let my work and my leadership and everything I do in the locker room behind the scenes show. Having the opportunity to do that, it's a blessing," Watson said. "I just put it all in God's hands and [let him] continue to write these stories and these opportunities I've got."

The Browns now head into the bye week and return with three consecutive home games. Cleveland is 4-0 at home this season.

articles.title: NFL: Patrick Mahomes has a new star, Kirk Cousins' emotional story continues and Christian McCaffrey lights up the Dallas Cowboys - NFL Sunday Review
articles.summary: NFL Sunday Review - we reflect on Week 10 in the NFL as Emmett Johnson announced himself as a new star on the Kansas City Chiefs, Kirk Cousins capped a memorable return for the Minnesota Vikings and Christian McCaffrey dominated in the San Francisco 49ers' win over the Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body:
It is the easiest story in the NFL to get behind. A 38-year-old Kirk Cousins, written off more times than he can count, deemed deep into the back nine of his career, coming back to a hero's welcome to spearhead a playoff charge while lighting a fire under an offense in desperate need of inspiration. His inspiration.

He is football's lovable goof, with the unpretentious, unflashy dad clothes and a 'down with the kids' willingness to sling on Justin Jefferson's chains should it lift his teammates. He is also now Minnesota's great hope of rewarding defensive mastery with an attack capable of competing in January football.

The Vikings were limping behind Kyler Murray, limping behind Carson Wentz but sitting a coveted 6-2, and on Tuesday rolled the dice by trading to bring back Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders.

It was three years ago that Cousins played the final game of his first chapter with the Vikings when he tore his Achilles tendon in Week Eight against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. On Sunday he was back where it ended - but could it yet be where it all started again?

Cousins, who had revived his starting career as mentor to No 1 pick Mendoza in Las Vegas, finished 21 of 31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in his first game back as the Vikings stunned the Packers 30-10.

His start featured a perfectly placed sideline strike between two defenders to a reception-starved Justin Jefferson on third-and-second in the first quarter, and so too a high-level tight-window bullet to Myles Price for a 38-yard touchdown catch-and-run on third-and-23.

It would become Jefferson's best game of the season as he made eight catches from nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns, Cousins' reconnecting with one of the stars of the league having seen him suffer for the first half of the season.

Much of the debate and, at times, criticism around Cousins throughout his career has been the shortage of point guard ability as a needle-moving creator. The Patrick Mahomes' and Josh Allens and Joe Burrows and Lamar Jacksons of the world have unfortunately heightened that bar for all quarterbacks across the league. But what has never been in doubt with Cousins is the efficiency at which he feeds his best players, and at which he moves the ball and at which he can accentuate an offense's strengths without being spectacular. Spectacular isn't exactly needed when there is a Brian Flores defense foaming at the mouth in wait of their chance to go hunting on the sideline.

In one game the Vikings looked a more polished, more accomplished operation behind Cousins, and alongside that came another rampant defensive play that saw Minnesota sack Jordan Love eight times.

In the first half alone they produced five sacks, 12 pressures, one interception and one fumble recovery, including sacks on back-to-back plays at the end of the second quarter. Their sixth sack then arrived on the very first play from scrimmage after the break, followed by the third of their four turnovers when Dallas Turner recover a wayward snap.

They were frightening, and the perfect complement once Cousins had helped the Vikings get on top early. The impact was evidenced through the time of possession, Cousins' offense holding the ball for 17.55 minutes in the first half and 35.16 a week on since the Vikings mustered just 17 minutes and 28 seconds of possession against the Bills. What a difference some respite for one of the league's most potent defenses makes.

There was a nice moment in the second half when former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees paid tribute to Cousins' communication at the line of scrimmage, where he shifted personnel and changed the play like an orchestra conductor. It was long-lost control and assurance under center.

Cousins later executed a trick play that saw him pump fake left and the swivel to pump fake to his right before tossing to Gavin Bartholomew over the middle of the field for a touchdown. For Kevin O'Connell to dial up a play like that just days after Cousins' arrival is testament to the footballing brain now leading Minnesota's offense.

"It was emotional coming to this stadium three years ago, tearing my Achilles here. It's been a tough three years, just grateful for the opportunity to play here, grateful for my teammates and what they did to make this outcome possible.

"It's been a tough three years. There's more of the story to be written," said Cousins post-game, his voice cracking several times."

Cousins won just one playoff game in six seasons during his first stint with the Vikings, before signing a four-year $180m contract with the Atlanta Falcons in 2024, only to be bench for Michael Penix Jr in his first season. He was then released in March earlier this year before landing in Las Vegas as something of a bridge towards their new era under Mendoza.

What looked like a declining career hurtling towards its end is instead flirting with one final twist.

Patrick Mahomes' new friends are alright. The Kansas City Chiefs were without their best player this season in Kenneth Walker III on Sunday; it did not matter. The absence of last season's Super Bowl MVP paved the way for an increased role for fifth-round rookie running back Emmett Johnson, who capitalised emphatically with 22 carries for 101 yards and six catches for 70 yards and two scores through the air as Kansas City beat the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 in a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes. Johnson showcased his menu of evasive manoeuvres in the open field with a clinic in tackle-missing jukes and the yards-after-catch threat primed to see him become one of Andy Reid's favourite weapons over the second half of the season.

There was also a debut for wide receiver Josh Downs, who had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown in his first game since arriving via a trade from the Indianapolis Colts. It's been a long time since Mahomes and the Chiefs posed a consistent vertical threat but Downs could prove an answer to as much. Mahomes completed seven of 12 attempts on passes of 10-plus air yards for 206 yards and three touchdowns, while going three of six on attempts of 20-plus yards for 132 yards and two scores. The Chiefs offense is clicking.

Denzel Ward is playing at an All-Pro level. It is hard to be one of the best players on the league for so long on a team that has been bad for so long; Myles Garrett did it in Cleveland, and Denzel Ward is still doing it. He stepped up when the Browns needed him most on Sunday with a stunning diving pass break-up against Xavier Hutchinson to deny the Houston Texans with 30 seconds left in Cleveland's 27-24 victory. Ward allowed just four receptions for 16 yards from nine targets on Sunday while lining up against Nico Collins in man coverage on 10 of 11 routes, according to Next Gen Stats. Pat Surtain II may still hold the honour of top dog in the eyes of many, but Ward will feel he holds a strong argument as being the best corner in football.

There are encouraging signs for Fernando Mendoza. The Raiders ushered in a new chapter this weekend as No 1 overall Draft pick Mendoza led his side out against the Seattle Seahawks in his first regular season start following Cousins' trade to the Vikings. It started strongly with a touchdown run on his opening possession before Mike Macdonald dialled the pressure up a notch on defense in the second half as the Raiders offense suffered without star weapon Brock Bowers. He went 11 of 13 for 90 yards through the air in the first half, before managing just six of 16 for 53 yards following the interval. Mendoza finished the game 17 of 29 passing for 143 yards, zero touchdowns and zero turnovers while being sacked six times. Facing the league's best defense always beckoned as a baptism of fire, so the shortage of interceptions or apparent ball security issues was a plus point.

Brock Purdy is a top five quarterback in the NFL. For somebody so often pigeonholed as a 'system quarterback', he sure does do a lot of good outside of the system. Purdy continues to showcase an elite ability to extend plays and create outside of the pocket, perhaps best epitomised by the 74-yard McCaffrey touchdown catch-and-run that saw him side-step a near-certain sack, slide to his left, cut back inside and fire a dart to his open running back. Poise in the face of chaos and a ground threat that makes him dangerous off-script. Purdy finished the game 22 of 28 for 389 yards and three touchdowns with a 154.5 passer rating. He is in the MVP hunt and playing at a level among the premier play-callers in football. By now, though, he knows his true judgement comes around playoff time.

Christian McCaffrey: If you thought injury setbacks had zapped the juice in the 49ers running back, think again. McCaffrey went off for 223 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to tear apart of hobbling Cowboys defense, which surrendered a franchise-worst 584 yards at home. McCaffrey's 161 receiving yards were the most by a running back in a game since Jamaal Charles' 195 in 2013, while he is the first 49ers player with 200 scrimmage yards and three scores in a regular season game since Jerry Rice in 1995.

Parker Washington: Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen called him the best player on the field, and a man possessed. The Tennessee Titans could not live with Parker Washington as the Jags receiver took another major step closer towards a bumper new contract with a career-best seven catches for 152 yards and a touchdown in his side's 40-23 win. One play saw him put Alontae Taylor in a blender with another clinic in route-running, another play saw him levitate to haul in Trevor Lawrence's pass at the sideline, and another saw him race free for a 50-yard catch-and-run. His outstanding season continues.

Mike Vrabel : On more than one occasion on Sunday, the camera captured Mike Vrabel closing his eyes in excruciating thought at the sight of another setback for his Patriots, be it an injury or a pre-snap penalty. The game was over before it ever really began for last year's beaten Super Bowl finalists, Drake Maye departing after the opening drive through injury and a sputtering offense later losing AJ Brown in the latest disruption to what is threatening to become a nightmare maiden season in New England. They are 5-5 with the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings and Kansas City Chiefs coming up over the next month; their season is teetering on the edge.

Aidan Hutchinson: Perhaps it is unfair to kick a man when he is down, but it is hard to overlook a game-ending, potentially season-ending injury caused by a celebration. Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson is feared to have suffered a serious knee injury after landing awkwardly during a post-sack celebration on the opening drive of New England's defeat to the Lions in Munich. It was the same play that saw Maye suffer his own game-halting injury, with neither returning to the field. His absence would leave Detroit without their star edge rusher heading into the second half of their playoff charge

Player of the Weekend - Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions

Jahmyr Gibbs is a familiar resident in this slot, but he is impossible to ignore as the clear frontrunner for Offensive Player of the Year through 10 weeks. The Lions running back was at his scintillating best in Munich as he put up 252 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns to torch the Patriots defense, his 62 career touchdowns breaking Terrell Davis' record for most by a player through his first four seasons in NFL history. He is not only the perfect cocktail of speed and shiftiness, but one of the smartest crease detectors in football. He runs hard, he runs fast, he runs with high-powered intelligence as the focal point of Drew Petzing's Lions offense. Another clinic, this time on European soil, to extend his lead as the NFL leader in scrimmage yards.

The 49ers and the Cowboys go way back as one of the NFL's most storied rivalries between two of football's most prestigious franchises. They renewed their dislike to the sight of record numbers as they combined for a series-high 86 points, with San Francisco beating Dallas 46-40 to improve to 8-1 on the season. While the 49ers flexed their offensive power, in doing so there were more glaring concerns over the Cowboys and a defense ranked third worst in yards allowed. Dak Prescott threw five touchdown passes, three to George Pickens, as the Cowboys put up 439 yards of offense, only to come out second best. Purdy produced two scoring strikes to McCaffrey and one to Deebo Samuel.

"The second half was unacceptable; tackling was atrocious, you can't give up three explosive plays of over 65 yards for touchdowns and expect to win. Totally unacceptable defense in the second half," said Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer.

articles.title: Howe It Happened: Mason McCormick Injury Sinks Steelers Beyond Bengals Blowout
articles.summary: CINCINNATI, Ohio — Late in the first half of a 38-18 road loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday — […]
articles.body:
CINCINNATI, Ohio — Late in the first half of a 38-18 road loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday — of the variety that commands much more than a little soul-searching — with the Pittsburgh Steelers trailing by 17 and having had yet to dent the scoreboard, Aaron Rodgers was bowled over.

The hosts' first of six sacks on the night brought out Chris Boswell for a 45-yard field goal, which was met 1:16 later by Joe Burrow 's third touchdown pass of the night, casting Mike McCarthy 's team into the locker room with a 24-3 deficit and the appallingly injured Mason McCormick on its mind.

The Sunday night showdown with the driver's seat of the AFC North in the balance instead took on the form of a ritualistic sacrifice, one that purely served to show the visitors that, although the two teams that took the field dwell in the same division, the same doesn't go for leagues.

Steelers fans who made the trip and spattered an ocean of white were made to watch as their team was mercilessly yanked apart, limb by limb. Maybe to salvage whatever of the experience they could — or, more desperately, hoping for a rally — more than a few remained into the fourth quarter. Many Cincinnati faithful, looking to beat the traffic and tired from partying, marched for the exits before others donned in black and gold.

🚨🚨WARNING: GRAPHIC INJURY🚨🚨 #STEELERS OL MASON MCCORMICK HAS SUFFERED A GRUESOME LOWER-LEG INJURY. Medical personnel brought out an air cast and a cart for McCormick after his leg appeared to bend awkwardly. This looks extremely serious. 🙏🙏🙏 pic.twitter.com/hgL8XhMHYD — MLFootball (@MLFootball) November 16, 2026

🚨🚨WARNING: GRAPHIC INJURY🚨🚨 #STEELERS OL MASON MCCORMICK HAS SUFFERED A GRUESOME LOWER-LEG INJURY. Medical personnel brought out an air cast and a cart for McCormick after his leg appeared to bend awkwardly. This looks extremely serious. 🙏🙏🙏 pic.twitter.com/hgL8XhMHYD

MLFootball (@MLFootball) November 16, 2026

Steelers fans at home had the luxury of clicking their TVs off, if not zipping a projectile through them first. With under five minutes to go in the third quarter, Rodgers had all of six completions and 22 passing yards. He finished 15-for-29 for 143 yards and two touchdowns, both of which came with the contest essentially already decided.

Frequently facing press coverage, receiver DK Metcalf was held without a reception until the fourth quarter. Running back Jaylen Warren , who's been the offense's engine this season, was limited to 15 yards on seven carries.

"We kinda shot ourselves in the foot with a couple of plays, and couldn't really get going and didn't hit any passes," Rodgers said. "We just couldn't get anything going on offense for a long time."

Just nine of Burrow's 44 throws skidded off the grass as he piled up 409 yards and four touchdowns through the air. Superstar wideout Ja'Marr Chase reeled in 11 of those passes for 231 yards. A handful of those flew over Pittsburgh cornerback Asante Samuel Jr. , who had a night he'd rather forget. Only once did the Steelers' defense sack Burrow, too.

It's tough to argue, though, that McCormick didn't have the worst night of anyone involved.

If you're squeamish, it's probably not something you want to watch back, but words never really do these sorts of injuries justice.

Rodgers dropped into a pocket on a third-and-8 from the Bengals' 18-yard line, hoping to grasp closer before halftime.

Trying to fend off bull rushing Bengals defensive tackle Jonathan Allen, McCormick, the Steelers' left guard, lost the high ground and couldn't dig his feet back in as the two hugged, with Allen's arms jammed under McCormick's armpits. The Steelers' offensive tackles — Troy Fautanu and Max Iheanachor — had walled off Rodgers, taking care of their assignments with their backs by then turned to the end zone being defended.

The league's elder statesman saw Allen pushing toward him, though, and just as he stepped up to seek refuge, McCormick's right ankle buckled. Falling backward in agony, he rolled over Rodgers, too. As the signal-caller peeled himself off the ground, McCormick reached for his crooked leg.

Soon enough, teammates noticed why McCormick wasn't getting up. They dropped to a knee right away. More joined as trainers applied an air cast while waiting for the cart to wheel over. The love that the Steelers have for McCormick, McCarthy said, was evident.

"We'll speak on that when the time is right," McCarthy said in regards to an update on the severity of the injury.

This season, McCormick had flipped to the left side of the line alongside Fautanu. The two have each stressed that there's nobody they'd rather work in tandem with.

"It made a lot of us sick to our stomach," said Fautanu, who spoke to McCormick in the trainer's room after the game. "Seeing stuff like that, I had never seen anything like that before, but obviously prayers up for Mase, just making sure we're checking on the person, not really the player right now."

Fourth-year veteran Spencer Anderson stepped in, pointing out afterward that McCormick's leadership is why he's a team player representative on the NFL Players Association board. Inside linebacker Patrick Queen called McCormick, "a solid heartbeat on the offense, a guy that everybody on the team loves and can turn to, whether you need a laugh, or you need a pep talk — or whatever it is — that's the guy."

Having been part of why he has emerged as one of the NFL's most electric ballcarriers, Warren was crushed to see McCormick go down.

"We know it's the nature of the game, but we don't like to see that happen to our own guy — or anyone, for that matter," Warren said. "He was one of the leaders on offense."

Center Zach Frazier , who plays to McCormick's right, said "he's been playing lights out. He's obviously very important to us, and it hurts us not having him out there. It just sucks."

Anderson spoke to McCormick's toughness, a trait that teammates drew from up front.

"I would imagine he'd be back next week just because of the kind of guy he is, but obviously, he's gotta assess what the injury is," Anderson said.

Fautanu became emotional talking about his bond with McCormick, who figures to be out for a considerable amount of time.

"The amount of," Fautanu said before pausing for a moment and scanning over the locker room. "Work, and just the presence that he brings to this offense and this O-line room, it's a big loss, man. … I know his presence is still gonna be felt."

articles.title: Evening at the improv? Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey make sure 49ers, fans enjoyed show
articles.summary: One of the 49ers' biggest plays Sunday didn't happen by design. Instead, QB Brock Purdy and running back Christian McCaffrey winged it to produce a 74-yard T...
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas - The offensive explosion began with improvisation.

On Sunday, with the San Francisco 49ers trailing by six points and facing 3rd-and-8 at their 26-yard line, one play away from punting for the second time in their first four possessions, head coach Kyle Shanahan called a play in which wide receiver Keenan Allen was quarterback Brock Purdy 's first read.

But Allen, running an in-breaking route nine yards downfield, was blanketed by cornerback Joey Porter. Purdy looked to his left to his second read, wideout Deebo Samuel . Nope. Covered. Meanwhile, Purdy's pocket was crumbling. Linebacker Shemar James blitzed. So did safety Caleb Downs. Purdy's internal clock went off.

"I felt like I sort of had to get going," Purdy said.

What happened next opened the floodgates in the 49ers' 46-40 win in which they gained 584 yards, the fifth-most in franchise history, and became the first team with three offensive touchdowns of 65-plus yards since 2000.

As Purdy raced to his right, prepared to try to scramble for a first down, running back Christian McCaffrey made it a two-man improv act. McCaffrey's assignment on a play in which tight end George Kittle and wide receiver Jordan Watkins also ran routes didn't foreshadow glory.

"He was in protection (blocking)," Shanahan said.

After McCaffrey leaned his right shoulder into defensive tackle Kenny Clark, he stopped for a split second, surrounded by three offensive linemen, before realizing Purdy was keeping the play alive. Scramble-drill mode.

"It's just some backyard football," McCaffrey said.

McCaffrey, in the middle of the field, near the line of scrimmage, initially broke to his right, into the flat, but he was running with James, who was chasing Purdy toward the sideline. McCaffrey instinctively cut upfield to daylight, splitting two defenders, just as Purdy had decided to try to run for the first down.

"There's a point where it's like, 'All right, I think I can try to use my legs now at this moment,'" Purdy said. "And I was going to do that."

At full speed, Purdy, seeing McCaffrey all alone around the 35-yard line, violently slammed on the brakes, just a yard away from crossing the line of scrimmage.

"It's those little decisions that you make in games," McCaffrey said. "For Brock to not scramble - to not just surrender the play - but to keep it alive. That's a big deal."

It was six-point decision. Purdy tossed a floater to McCaffrey, who caught the ball at the 49ers' 41-yard line and received an escort from tight end George Kittle as he sprinted 59 yards untouched to finish a 74-yard connection that gave the 49ers a 17-16 lead as Fox announcers Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady laughed at the improbability of their improv magic.

There's an NFL axiom: It's not the Xs and the Os, it's the Jimmies and the Joes. Shanahan acknowledged Purdy, the NFL's passer rating king, and McCaffrey, who has the most touchdown receptions by running back in league history, bailed him out.

"That's an example," Shanahan said, "of making the play better than the one we called."

It was also the start of an offensive onslaught. Before Purdy connected with McCaffrey, the 49ers had averaged 5.4 yards on their first 25 offensive plays. They finished by averaging 13.1 yards on their final 34 snaps, gaining 445 yards in the final 32-plus minutes while scoring 36 points.

Fittingly, the players who got the party started played the starring roles. McCaffrey scored three touchdowns and had 223 total yards, including 161 receiving, the most by a running back since 2013, according to the Associated Press. Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes for a career-high 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions, posting a 154.5 rating that was the second-highest of his 58-start career.

Right tackle Colton McKivitz shook his head when discussing the duo that did in Dallas, which allowed the most yards in a home game in the franchise's 67-season history.

"We've got a quarterback who can do it all, including making ridiculous plays, getting out of the pocket and moving around if there's pressure," McKivitz said. "And then, obviously, a running back who is a generational talent. One of the greatest running backs, rushing and receiving, to ever play this game."

With the 49ers clinging to a 38-32 lead with 3:32 left, Purdy and McCaffrey delivered the dagger on 2nd-and-10 from the 49ers' 34. The Cowboys sent an all-out blitz, leaving McCaffrey with the upper hand in a comical mismatch.

Pass rusher Von Miller, 37, was in coverage as Purdy connected with McCaffrey in the middle of the field, at the 49ers' 40, and McCaffrey wasn't touched for the final 60 yards as Miller hopelessly gave chase.

"I was like, 'Oh, Christian's there, great matchup,'" Purdy said.

Said Shanahan: "We got the right defensive look. They (blitzed), we scatted everyone out and, when you do that, the back gets a route on the D-end."

It was a great play call. And that made Purdy and McCaffrey's second long-touchdown connection the opposite of their first.

Shanahan was asked about the call that led to the improv act. What was the initial design of that play?

articles.title: NFL: Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson out for rest of season after suffering knee injury during celebration
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions are set to be without star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the rest of the season after he suffered a torn ACL while celebrating a sack on Drake Maye during Sunday's win over the New England Patriots at Munich's Allianz Arena in Germany
articles.body:
Hutchinson leaped in the air but went straight to the ground after landing. He immediately grabbed his right knee, staying down before eventually walking to the blue tent for evaluation.

He then walked gingerly to the locker room and didn't return to the game.

NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported Monday that initial tests revealed Hutchinson sustained a torn ACL that will see him miss the rest of the season.

Hutchinson had sacked Maye on third down at the Detroit 15-yard line to end New England's opening drive, which saw Andy Borregales then kick a 33-yard field goal.

Maye also exited the game after the same play and is feared to have suffered a season-ending fractured ankle , with further tests expected upon his return to the United States.

The Lions went on to win the game 35-10 at Munich's Allianz Arena as the Patriots offense capitulated behind backup quarterback Tommy DeVito.

But it came at a major cost, with Detroit now set to resume their bid to reach a first Super Bowl minus their star pass rusher for the rest of the way.

Hutchinson has six sacks so far this year along with 50 pressures, following on from a 2025 season in which he led the team with a career-high 14.5 sacks.

Defensive end Derrick Moore impressed in Hutchinson's absence Sunday with two of the team's four sacks, with Alim McNeill also adding six pressures and increasing his sack tally to 6.5 on the year.

Hutchinson missed 12 games during the 2024 campaign after breaking his tibia and fibula.

Next up for the Lions, who are 7-2, is a meeting with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before they host the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving.
